items.finding: Round2 anchor 7
items.reason: Checked the saved article’s Methods, Results 1, Results 2.2.1, Table 2, Discussion and cited reference entries 33, 35–37. items.finding: Round2 anchor 11
items.reason: The substantive reported counts and cautions are supported, including the unreconciled printed 28% hospital figure and contradictory Toxreg prose. With inventory membership as the reference, 761/1,212=62.8% and 761/(761+419)=64.5%; the paper prints these in the opposite sensitivity/positive-predictive-value order. The 30 inventory omissions and inconsistent totals prevent treating the resulting labels as validated causal accuracy. items.finding: Round2 anchor 13
items.reason: Verified printed p. 274 Methods and p. 276 discordant-case Results (PDF pp. 2 and 4). The 37 natural-coded OMI poisonings, 16 heart-disease cases, 17 other-injury cases, 15 OMI natural deaths coded 305 in vital statistics and 13 never-reported in-state cases match. Independently calculated 16/37=43.24%. The authors say the 37 typically had poisoning in Part II only; individual certificate texts for the 15 code-305 deaths are not given. The proposed statement correctly treats use/abuse wording as an inference and includes non-drug poisons.

items.finding: Round2 anchor 14
items.reason: Counts, printed endpoint/aggregate Table 1 intervals and the unlinked projection method are verified in the supplied PDF, including 300 dpi Fig. 1/Table 1. The main text does not explicitly discuss or exclude searching a separate Record of Inquest conclusion entry; remove that unsupported specificity. Also distinguish printed projections from exact recomputation: 122/416=29.3269%, and 574/(294/416)=812.1905, whereas the paper prints 813. A Wilson interval from 122/416 transforms to 766.94–868.05, reproducing the Table 1 endpoints after rounding. The full annual NPSUM denominators and supplements are absent, so 2022/aggregate intervals were transcribed, not independently regenerated. Independently recomputed six aggregate missing shares, 96.8306% multiple-drug detection and the 50.8648% heroin/morphine increase over ONS. There are additional source-table inconsistencies recorded in the notes; do not silently repair them.

items.finding: Round2 anchor 16
items.reason: The six category counts, default-overdose rule and independent two-reader/medical-confirmation procedure are verified, and the counts sum to 1,037. That characterization is an editorial inference from the default rule, not an author finding or a validated mathematical bound; surrounding statement/magnitude wording should be changed accordingly. The negative-toxicology caveat is in the final Discussion paragraph on printed p. 73, outside the proposed pp. 68–70 locator. The complete replacement below fixes both content and location.
